cards.text: Jesus has sent His twelve disciples out two by two, and they're healing the sick and driving out demons (Mark 6:7-13). Now Jesus' name has become well known, and the news reaches King Herod, ruler of Galilee (Luke 3:1).

cards.question: Some people have an explanation for the miraculous powers at work in Jesus: He's a man who has risen from the dead. Which man?

cards.text: John the Baptist is the man who baptized Jesus (Mark 1:9). Others say Jesus is Elijah, the prophet of Israel (1 Kings 17:1), and still others say He's a prophet like one of the prophets of old, so this is the office break room on a Monday: EVERYBODY'S got a theory.

cards.question: King Herod hears all the theories about Jesus and lands on Elijah.

cards.text: Herod says, "John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!" Hold up, friend, BEHEADED?!
Let's rewind, because Herod himself had ordered John arrested, bound and locked in prison. It all had to do with a woman named Herodias, whom Herod had married.

cards.question: Before Herod married Herodias, she was the wife of Herod's ___ Philip.
John the Baptist had something to say to Herod about his marriage to Herodias. What had John been telling Herod?

answers.text: It's not lawful to have your brother's wife
It's not lawful to marry without a priest
It's not lawful to hold a wedding on the Sabbath

cards.question: Herodias lets it go when John says Herod's marriage to her isn't lawful.

cards.text: Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him, but she couldn't pull it off. Me, I can't even hold a grudge against the junk drawer, and that thing kept me in the dark for YEARS.

cards.question: Herodias wants John the Baptist dead, but she can't make it happen. What's stopping her?

answers.text: Herod feared John and protected him
The prison guards refused her orders

cards.question: Herod knew John was a righteous and holy man. John's words greatly perplexed Herod, so Herod stopped listening to him.

cards.text: Then comes Herod's birthday... and Herodias finally gets her opportunity. Herod throws a banquet for his nobles, his military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
The daughter of Herodias comes in and dances, and she pleases Herod and his guests. Then Herod gets generous, and I mean REAL generous.

cards.question: King Herod is so pleased with the daughter of Herodias that he makes her a promise and swears to it. What does he offer her?

answers.text: Whatever she asks up to half his kingdom
A palace of her own anywhere in Galilee
Gold and jewels from the royal treasury

cards.text: Up to half his kingdom, and I get nervous promising a baker an extra scoop of sprinkles! The girl steps out to get some advice: "What should I request?"

cards.question: Before the daughter of Herodias makes her request to King Herod, she steps out to ask someone what she should request. Who does she ask?

cards.text: And her mother answers, "The head of John the Baptist." Herodias has been waiting a long time for this one.

cards.question: The daughter of Herodias takes her time thinking it over before she goes back to the king.

cards.text: At once she hurries back to the king: "I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately." That's her mother's answer word for word, friend, plus a platter and a deadline.

cards.question: King Herod hears the girl's request for John's head, and he is consumed with ___.
King Herod is heartbroken, but he still won't refuse the girl's request. Why not?

answers.text: Because of his oaths and his guests
Because he feared what Herodias would do
Because John had insulted the girl

cards.text: So without delay, the king commands that John's head be brought in. He sends an executioner, who goes and beheads John in the prison.

cards.question: The executioner brings John's head on a platter to the daughter of Herodias, and she gives it to her mother.
John the Baptist's disciples hear what happened to him. What do they do?

answers.text: Take his body and lay it in a tomb
Go to Herod's palace to confront him
Scatter and hide far outside Galilee

findings.problem: Saying Herodias 'has been waiting a long time' adds a duration the passage does not give. Mark says she held a grudge, wanted to kill John and later received an opportunity, but never says how long she waited.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card's observation that the girl repeats her mother's answer 'word for word' uses the mother's wording in Mark 6:24 as well as the girl's request in Mark 6:25. Citing only Mark 6:25 is too narrow; the card should cite Mark 6:24-25.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
